rows.label: P10 (new: PGQ-037, reparenting isn't an exercise)
rows.article: Reparenting isn't an exercise you finish
notes: Turn 76 (his message of 2026-10-19 00:55 UTC (experiments/t76-answers/JOEL-20261019-0055.md), "start workin on the innerSignalGraph queue"): PGQ-037 (reparenting isn't an exercise), from innerSignalGraph's queue, version 2026-10-18-r12 (authoring/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES.md at 55b2b0dd): a short paragraph of mine after my PGQ-012 paragraph, since the queue's place (after the guide's "Reparenting begins when the present-day person occupies an adult position") isn't in the article, and three versions of these sentences inside the PGQ-012 paragraph made it read AI alone (rounds t76a to t76c). The queue asks for one or two sentences; at 42 words it's under the gate's 50, so its check is the h1's. experiments/t76-guide/drafts/cs57x-a.txt. 42 words, so its check is the h1's: The Chicken-and-Egg Problem with it Human Written (0.031, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/0296c5e3-5a39-4d1c-8541-4b2ef12881cc (round t76d).

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-037)
beside.text: Reparenting isn't an exercise you do or finish; it's the ongoing relationship in which the adult you are now cares for, validates, protects and guides the younger, vulnerable part of you, through truthful boundaries, repair and everyday choices as much as through any meditation. Learning to feel safe inside while you say what you really feel, need and won't accept is that work, not a separate goal it might help with. Meditations, imagery, inner dialogue and affirmations are ways of practicing it, not its definition, its entry ticket or its scorecard: a session with no tears or relief doesn't mean nothing is happening, and the right words in a session don't by themselves mean it's done. Other help, such as people who support you or specialist care for physical pain, stays its own thing.

headings: # Borrow the Adult Before You Can Be the Adult
## Borrow Love—or Borrow the Perspective of Care

rows.label: P6 (new: PGQ-033, "if only I had X")
rows.article: And when you catch yourself thinking
notes: Turn 76 (his message of 2026-10-19 00:55 UTC (experiments/t76-answers/JOEL-20261019-0055.md), "start workin on the innerSignalGraph queue"): PGQ-033 ("if only I had X"), from innerSignalGraph's queue, version 2026-10-18-r12 (authoring/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES.md at 55b2b0dd): a short paragraph of mine after his P5, next to his gratitude part as the queue has it; the survey he remembered isn't cited, since no source has turned up (question 65). experiments/t76-guide/drafts/ag5b-c.txt. 43 words, so its check is the h1's: Borrow the Adult Before You Can Be the Adult with it Human Written (0.052, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/8c2a2d67-a543-4ae9-b265-19e3e3d27480 (round t76c), with the grounding's last sentence ("If it doesn't, the gratitude never shows up.").

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-033)
beside.text: Gratitude that waits for conditions never arrives. When someone says they could be grateful “if only I had X,” ask what they would need before they could feel love or gratitude, and whether that list ever ends. The owner recalls a survey in which almost nobody wished for happiness directly; no source has been found for it, so don't cite it unless one turns up. Research on “miswanting” (Gilbert and Wilson, 2000), on how people mispredict what will make them happy, makes a related point and can be cited instead if the owner wants a source.

headings: # Building Trust With Your Little One
## Not Every Hero Wears A Cape

rows.label: P6 (new: PGQ-038, keeping yourself safe is part of the work)
rows.article: Keeping yourself safe counts as one of those acts
notes: Turn 76 (his message of 2026-10-19 00:55 UTC (experiments/t76-answers/JOEL-20261019-0055.md), "start workin on the innerSignalGraph queue"): PGQ-038 (keeping yourself safe is part of the work), from innerSignalGraph's queue, version 2026-10-18-r12 (authoring/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES.md at 55b2b0dd): a short paragraph of mine at the end of this h2, since the queue's place, right after "Warmth can come later.", is inside P3 here, and P4 picks up P3's last word; it keeps the guide's permission not to call it reparenting ("if you like seeing it that way"). The queue asks for one or two sentences; at 49 words it's under the gate's 50, so its check is the h2's and the h1's; four longer versions read AI alone (rounds t76a to t76c). experiments/t76-guide/drafts/hero6-e.txt. 49 words, so its checks are its h2's and h1's: Not Every Hero Wears A Cape Human Written (0.094, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/b48c7893-905a-41a2-b09d-a0b594245c0e; Building Trust With Your Little One Human Written (0.032, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/b48feb12-3db6-4e54-a83c-621fa8e36c94 (round t76d).

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-038)
beside.text: Keeping yourself safe in everyday ways, such as leaving a place where you're being hurt, resting, keeping a boundary or arranging company or a safer place, is the adult you are now protecting the younger, vulnerable part of you: when that way of seeing it fits you, it is reparenting, not a separate therapy to finish before the real work starts. That stays true when the step involves someone else: asking a friend to come along, or staying with someone for a while, is still your own step. Help from outside, such as a doctor, crisis care, a shelter, the police or the help another person gives, stays its own thing: it can serve the same care, but it isn't an exercise, and reparenting doesn't replace it.

headings: # When the Adult Voice Feels Fake
### When the Urge to Escape Arrives

rows.label: P13 (new: PGQ-027, urgent care during unbearable pain)
rows.article: Physical pain can bring on the urge to escape

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-027)
beside.text: During an unbearable physical-pain episode, caring for yourself may mean contacting local urgent medical services for assessment and possible pain relief—even when earlier investigations found no clear answer—rather than relying on a short-lived strategy known to worsen your condition.

rows.article: But what if the attacks come almost every day
notes: Turn 76 (his message of 2026-10-19 00:55 UTC (experiments/t76-answers/JOEL-20261019-0055.md), "start workin on the innerSignalGraph queue"): PGQ-029 (frequent severe pain: a specialist and a written flare plan, with the new or severe signs that still mean going in), from innerSignalGraph's queue, version 2026-10-18-r12 (authoring/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES.md at 55b2b0dd) and the guide's next paragraph ("If severe pain attacks happen almost every day"); the France example compressed, as the queue asks. experiments/t76-guide/drafts/ue29-b.txt. Alone Human Written (0.221), https://www.pangram.com/history/f82c2224-b62b-477a-85bd-66920af677c4 (round t76c); the h1 with both pain paragraphs as above (round t76f).

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-029)
beside.text: Severe frequent pain deserves a continuing specialist treatment pathway and a written plan for predictable flares, with acute services as a proportionate backup. Prior normal tests need not make pain imaginary. In France a doctor can request SDC assessment and justify a priority referral if warranted; no guaranteed appointment or medication. Specialist-appropriate options are not diagnostic proofs.

headings: # Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

rows.label: P5 (new: PGQ-032, a drug peak that changes nothing)
rows.article: And then there's the peak that changes nothing
notes: Turn 76 (his message of 2026-10-19 00:55 UTC (experiments/t76-answers/JOEL-20261019-0055.md), "start workin on the innerSignalGraph queue"): PGQ-032 (a drug peak that changes nothing; his example of 2026-10-14 23:26 UTC), from innerSignalGraph's queue, version 2026-10-18-r12 (authoring/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES.md at 55b2b0dd): a paragraph of mine right after the beautiful-state paragraph, where the queue has it, with no public figure named (question 64). experiments/t76-guide/drafts/as4b-f.txt. Alone Human Written (0.031), https://www.pangram.com/history/f4093935-c708-4a05-b9c7-20cb9ba041a0; the h1 with it Human Written (0.073, high), https://www.pangram.com/history/83d69825-fc68-4c58-986e-c0f9ca3c56f7 (round t76c). as4b-d read Human too (alone 0.0078, the h1 0.070; round t76a); as4b-f has the grounding's fixes: the anger set up before it's asked about, and the last sentence split so the peak is said not to be that love.

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-032)
beside.text: The owner's example: someone who wants enlightenment together with money, partners and everything else, as one package, can reach a drug peak (ketamine, say) without letting go of a single attachment or of the anger. A peak reached that way is not the unconditional love the practice is after, and wanting everything is the conditional gratitude the practice works on. Help readers see it for themselves rather than preach it.

beside.label: The queue's point (PGQ-028)
